terminal_objective: Prove one single cognitive identity can take a difficult real computer-work goal from ambiguous request to verified finished result while using durable Brain state and resuming after a session boundary.
mission_requirements: interpret a real consequential goal rather than a synthetic predicate
inspect existing context and constraints from Project Brain
discover and use tools/apps appropriate to the task
perform meaningful computer actions in browser or professional software
create or modify a consequential artifact or software result
inspect the actual result and detect at least one real issue if present
correct the result rather than merely report the issue
persist mission state and evidence to Project Brain before a session boundary
resume from persisted state without repeating completed work
verify the final result independently from its own planning narrative
write durable evidence and lessons back to Project Brain
anti_shortcuts: do not borrow persistence proof from a deterministic worker
do not borrow cognition proof from another chat
do not compose booleans from different identities
do not count benchmark completion as mission completion
do not promote from one narrow HTTP or repository task
success_definition: The exact same worker identity demonstrably completes the full cognitive and persistent loop on the real mission.
